Inflation factors of the imputed mean and SD

Source: R/sdf.R
inflation_factors.Rd

The inflation factors (IF) of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026): the ratio of the standard deviation of the imputed mean to that of the sample mean, \(\kappa_\mu(n) = \mathrm{SD}(\hat\mu)/\mathrm{SD}(\bar X) = C_\mu(n)\sqrt n\), and of the imputed SD to that of the sample SD \(S\), \(\kappa_\sigma(n) = \mathrm{SD}(\hat\sigma)/\mathrm{SD}(S) = C_\sigma(n)/\sqrt{1 - b_S(n)^2}\), where \(b_S(n) = \sqrt{2/(n-1)}\,\Gamma(n/2)/\Gamma\{(n-1)/2\}\) is the bias factor of \(S\), \(E[S] = b_S(n)\sigma\). The factors \(C_\mu(n)\) and \(C_\sigma(n)\) are the exact ones of c_mu and c_sigma, from one exact moment set.

Usage

inflation_factors(
  n,
  scenario = c("S3", "S1", "S2", "S4", "S5"),
  version = c("blue", "wan_luo_shi"),
  type = 7
)

Arguments

n

Integer sample size: at least 3 under S1 and S2, 5 under S3 and S4, and 7 under S5, under the default quantile definition. Any such n is computed exactly; see Details. Another definition may need a larger \(n\): where two reported values are the same order statistic (type 3 at \(n = 5\) under S3, for example) the BLUE is not defined and is refused.

scenario

Character. One of "S1" (min, median, max), "S2" (three quartiles), "S3" (all five). McGrath 2023 labels; note Wan 2014's C2/C3 are S3/S2 respectively. Also "S4" (the quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles) and "S5" (all five with the two percentiles), the names of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026) for Scenarios 5 and 7 of Balakrishnan et al. (2022); only the BLUE ("blue") is defined for these two.

version

"blue" (default) for the BLUE of both, or "wan_luo_shi" for the estimators of Wan, Luo and Shi (Luo's mean; Wan's SD under S1 and S2, Shi's under S3). Under S4 and S5 only "blue" is defined.

type

The definition of the sample quantiles, an integer from 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7, R's default, unless a study states another.

Value

Named numeric vector: kappa_mu, kappa_sigma.

Details

Assumptions as in imputed_moments: iid normal data, the reported values following definition type. An IF of 1.2 means a 20% larger SD than that of the full-sample statistic.

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

inflation_factors(41, "S2")                       # the BLUE: about 1.076 and 1.651
#>    kappa_mu kappa_sigma 
#>    1.076399    1.651035 
inflation_factors(41, "S2", version = "wan_luo_shi")
#>    kappa_mu kappa_sigma 
#>    1.076399    1.652702 
inflation_factors(40, "S2")                       # an even n: interpolated quartiles, type 7
#>    kappa_mu kappa_sigma 
#>    1.070136    1.620424 
inflation_factors(21, "S4")                       # quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles
#>    kappa_mu kappa_sigma 
#>    1.028619    1.207533
